name: Lucy
first: First mission to the Jupiter Trojans; visits 11 bodies across 8 asteroids and their satellites in a single 12-year trajectory — a record number of objects on separate solar orbits
description: Lucy reaches for the L4 and L5 Lagrange clouds — populations of primordial asteroids leading and trailing Jupiter by 60°, believed to preserve material from the outer protoplanetary disc. Three Earth gravity assists (2022, 2024, 2030) shape a single trajectory that visits seven Trojan asteroids plus bonus main-belt targets. First asteroid encounter: 152830 Dinkinesh (2023-11-01, ~790 m), at which imaging revealed the contact-binary satellite Selam. Bonus main-belt: Donaldjohanson 2025-04. L4 swarm: Eurybates + moon Queta (2027-08), Polymele (2027-09), Leucus (2028-04), Orus (2028-11). After EGA-3 (2030-12), the trailing L5 swarm: Patroclus-Menoetius binary (2033-03) — the largest Trojan binary known, a fitting climax for the mission's namesake (Lucy the hominid fossil; Patroclus-Menoetius the two characters that fell together in the Iliad).

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: Atlas V 401 from Cape Canaveral SLC-41.

events.label: DINKINESH
events.note: 2023-11-01. First asteroid flyby — ~790 m main-belt body; satellite Selam (contact binary) discovered.

events.label: EGA-3
events.note: Final Earth assist 2030-12. Heads to L5 cloud.
